## Summary

- add `--gsp-input-ids` for the generated-shared-prefix dataset
- send raw random token IDs directly so the server skips tokenization before prefill
- keep input-ID cache entries separate from text-mode cache entries

This ports the change from HYGON-AI/sglang-das#315.

## Benchmarking note

When measuring the speedup, 用 `/generate` 或 `/v1/completions` 发；不要用 chat 接口，否则 chat template 等额外开销会让结果看起来“没快多少”。

nodes.body:
### CI failure triage

I dug into the failing checks on this PR — none of them are caused by the code changes here (only two benchmark files touched; Lint and all CPU stage-a jobs pass). Summary of root causes from the run logs:

| Failure | Root cause | Related to this PR? |
|---|---|---|
| PR Test Base — all `base-b-*` jobs CANCELLED | The `wait-for-base-b` step (wait-for-jobs action) timed out after ~17 min waiting for GPU runners and cascaded-cancelled the whole base-b batch. Infrastructure queueing — no test in that batch actually failed. | No |
| PR Test Extra (AMD) — `call-gate / pr-gate` | Gate log: `Missing required label 'run-ci-extra'. Add the label (e.g. via /tag-and-rerun-ci extra)`. The PR only carries `run-ci`. | No (config) |
| AMD `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd` (8) | `test/registered/observability/test_tracing.py::test_trace_level_0` — `AssertionError: 6 != 0 : Spans collected but expected none` (`/set_trace_level`, `/generate` spans). Observability flake. | No |
| AMD `stage-b-test-1-gpu-large-amd` (2) | `test/registered/basic_perf/test_score_api.py` — latency assertion `67.3s <= 60s` failed. Perf variance on the runner. | No |
| AMD `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` | `test/registered/e2e/quantization/test_quark_mxfp4.py` — accuracy `0.834 not greater than 0.85` on MI35X. | No |
| NPU `base-b-test-4-npu-a3 / run (0)`, XPU `stage-a-test-1-gpu-xpu` | Both failed in the "Run test" step; this PR doesn't touch NPU/XPU code paths. | No |

Could a maintainer please help with:

1. **Re-run the failed workflows** (Base / AMD / XPU / NPU) — the Base batch was cancelled by a runner-wait timeout, so it should pass on rerun; the AMD flakes are unrelated known-noisy tests.
2. **Add the `run-ci-extra` label** (or `/tag-and-rerun-ci extra`) so the Extra gate stops failing on the missing label.
3. **Take a look at the review** when convenient — the PR is currently stuck on REVIEW_REQUIRED.

Happy to address any feedback on the benchmark changes themselves. Thanks!

Thanks for the PR — sending raw ids for GSP is useful (it also makes the shared prefix exact at the token level, which the decode→re-encode text path doesn't guarantee). A few issues before merge:

**main already has this switch.** `--tokenize-prompt` (`serving.py`, "Use integer ids instead of string for inputs") is the existing global flag for this; `random-ids` honors it via `return_text=not tokenize_prompt`, and `async_request_sglang_generate` already sends `input_ids` for non-str prompts. GSP currently just asserts it off (`generated_shared_prefix.py:59`). Suggest dropping `--gsp-input-ids` and instead removing that assert + wiring `input_ids=args.tokenize_prompt` — that also inherits the existing `backend == "sglang"` guard and avoids two flags for the same thing.

**Must-fix**
1. `--gsp-num-turns > 1` + ids silently produces wrong traffic (inline below).
2. No backend guard: chat backends receive `list[int]` as `messages` (inline below).

**Nits**
- Stats are suppressed in ids mode, but `prompt_len = len(ids)` is exact there — totals/averages can still be printed (use `len()` instead of `tokenizer.encode`).
- No test: `test/registered/bench_fn/test_benchmark_datasets_api.py` already covers `random-ids` + `tokenize_prompt=True`; a GSP counterpart asserting `list[int]` prompts, `prompt_len == len(prompt)`, and rejection of multi-turn would cover this.

Rather than a new GSP-only flag, consider reusing the existing `--tokenize-prompt`: remove `assert not getattr(args, "tokenize_prompt", False)` above and use `input_ids=getattr(args, "tokenize_prompt", False)`. That matches `random-ids` and picks up the existing `--backend sglang` check in `serving.py`.

nodes.body: **must-fix**: with `--gsp-num-turns > 1`, each prompt becomes `List[List[int]]`. In `benchmark()`, `_normalize_round_messages(list[int])` returns `None`, so `is_multi_turn` is False and the multi-turn wrapper is skipped. The whole list-of-lists is then sent as `input_ids` to `/generate`, which the server treats as a *batch*: turn 1 = system+q1, turns 2..N = bare questions with no history. Results are wrong with no error. Please reject `num_turns > 1` together with ids mode at arg validation.

reviews.body:
Thanks for the PR — sending raw ids for GSP is useful (it also makes the shared prefix exact at the token level, which the decode→re-encode text path doesn't guarantee). A few issues before merge:

**main already has this switch.** `--tokenize-prompt` (`serving.py`, "Use integer ids instead of string for inputs") is the existing global flag for this; `random-ids` honors it via `return_text=not tokenize_prompt`, and `async_request_sglang_generate` already sends `input_ids` for non-str prompts. GSP currently just asserts it off (`generated_shared_prefix.py:59`). Suggest dropping `--gsp-input-ids` and instead removing that assert + wiring `input_ids=args.tokenize_prompt` — that also inherits the existing `backend == "sglang"` guard and avoids two flags for the same thing.

**Must-fix**
1. `--gsp-num-turns > 1` + ids silently produces wrong traffic (inline below).
2. No backend guard: chat backends receive `list[int]` as `messages` (inline below).

**Nits**
- Stats are suppressed in ids mode, but `prompt_len = len(ids)` is exact there — totals/averages can still be printed (use `len()` instead of `tokenizer.encode`).
- No test: `test/registered/bench_fn/test_benchmark_datasets_api.py` already covers `random-ids` + `tokenize_prompt=True`; a GSP counterpart asserting `list[int]` prompts, `prompt_len == len(prompt)`, and rejection of multi-turn would cover this.
